item.description: arXiv:2610.39644v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a quantitative criterion for local Lipschitz regularity of Sobolev maps in the sense of Korevaar and Schoen from finite-dimensional \(\RCD(K,N)\) spaces into complete \(\CAT(0)\) spaces, without assuming harmonicity. We quantify the failure of local energy minimality by the harmonic replacement potential, a dyadic sum of the square roots of normalized energy gaps between a map and its harmonic replacements. We prove that this potential, together with an averaged energy term, controls the minimal weak upper gradient pointwise, with constants depending only on the curvature-dimension bounds and the scale. In particular, local boundedness of the replacement potential implies that the map admits a locally Lipschitz representative.
item.dc:creator: Bang-Xian Han, Zeyu Wang

item.title: Symmetry and uniqueness of degree $-1$ minimizers of a chiral magnetic energy
item.description: arXiv:2610.39651v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the two-dimensional energy of a chiral magnet, consisting of the exchange energy, a bulk Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya interaction with constant $\kappa\ne0$, and the Zeeman energy in an applied field $h>0$. We prove that the minimizers of this energy among maps of degree $-1$ are exactly the translates of one axially symmetric Bloch skyrmion, whose helicity is determined by the sign of $\kappa$. This holds for $h \geq c \kappa^2$, where $c \in(\pi^2 / 16,1)$ is determined by the slope of the radial profile at the origin; in particular, it holds in the whole range $h\ge\kappa^2$, which answers a question raised by Melcher and by D\"oring and Melcher. The proof is a calibration argument. Using the profile of the skyrmion, we write the energy density of an arbitrary map as a weighted topological density, plus a divergence, plus a nonnegative remainder, and we show that this identity can be integrated for every map of finite energy. The method also gives the uniqueness of the monotone solution of the profile equation for $h\ge\kappa^2/2$.
item.dc:creator: Xiuqing Duan

item.title: A new sharp Sobolev inequality between the $Q$-curvature and the scalar curvature on Euclidean space
item.description: arXiv:2610.39659v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a sharp Sobolev-type inequality on $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\geq 5$, that interpolates between the second-order energy and a weighted first-order term. Specifically, we determine the sharp constant $S_{4,2}$ in the inequality \begin{equation*} \int_{\mathbb R^n} (\Delta u)^2\,dx \ge S_{4,2} \left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}|\nabla u|^{2}|u|^{\frac{4}{n-4}}\,dx\right)^{\frac{n-4}{n-2}}, \end{equation*} for any $u\in\dot H^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$, and we classify the cases of equality. This solves the problem of minimizing the total $Q$-curvature of among metrics on the sphere, conformal to the standard metric, with fixed total scalar curvature.
item.dc:creator: Rupert L. Frank, Yuxin Ge, Guofang Wang, Wei Wei

item.title: A sharp lower bound for torsional rigidity of convex domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.39666v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every bounded convex domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, we establish the following sharp inequality for torsional rigidity $$T(\Omega)\ge\frac{2(d+1)}{d}\int\limits_\Omega\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial\Omega)^2\dd x,$$ where $T(\Omega)=4\int\limits_\Omega u\dd x$ and $-\Delta u=1$ in $\Omega$, $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$. Equality holds for balls.
item.dc:creator: M. A. Perelmuter

item.title: The fundamental solution of a family of anisotropic fourth-order parabolic equations: small-time asymptotics and related Gaussian estimates
item.description: arXiv:2610.39686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the fundamental solutions of a class of uniformly elliptic fourth-order parabolic equations in two dimensions, whose principal symbols are not necessarily strongly convex. For constant-coefficient operators, we derive precise small-time asymptotic formulas along certain special directions. These formulas are obtained by the method of steepest descent and reveal the dependence of the asymptotic behavior on the coefficients of the symbol. We subsequently consider operators with bounded measurable coefficients, subject to Dirichlet boundary conditions, and establish Gaussian bounds for their fundamental solutions by means of Davies' exponential perturbation method. The exponential constant in these bounds is shown to be sharp, as a consequence of the constant-coefficient asymptotics.
item.dc:creator: Gerassimos Barbatis, Efstratios Karafylis

item.title: Unified transform method for nonautonomous linear evolution equations: rigorous analysis and qualitative theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.39698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Established herein is the rigorous extension of the celebrated Fokas unified transform method for linear evolution PDE with time-dependent coefficients. As illustrative examples, considered below and rigorously analysed in detail are non-homogeneous initial-boundary-value problems, formulated on the half-line, for the heat equation and the modified heat (also widely known as Barenblatt's pseudo-parabolic) equation with reaction terms and temporally varying coefficients. Solution formulae are derived formally via suitable implementation of the UTM, and rigorously verified a posteriori, in the classical sense. The latter task relies on complex-analytic tools and careful interpretation of the obtained integral representations. The explicit solutions established here are then used for investigating qualitative properties. These include regularity, boundary behavior near the axes of the domain as well as long-range and eventual periodicity asymptotics. Notably, smoothness of the solution up to the boundaries depends on compatibility conditions between initial, boundary and forcing data, into which interjected now are initial values of the coefficients. Further results pertaining to solution uniqueness, analyticity and controllability of the addressed problems are thence deduced in light of the preceding qualitative theory.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Chatziafratis, Spyridon Kamvissis, Alain Miranville, Tohru Ozawa

item.title: Optimality of the BCC lattice among 3D lattice quantizers
item.description: arXiv:2610.39705v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the problem of the best approximation (w.r.t. the optimal transport metric $W_p$, $p \in [1,\infty)$) of the three-dimensional Lebesgue measure on a domain of volume 1 by a discrete probability measure supported on a Bravais lattice. This problem is known as the quantization problem and it arises in numerical integration, electrical engineering, discrete geometry and materials science. As the lattice size tends to zero and the cardinality of the support of the discrete measure tends to infinity, this reduces to the following geometric optimization problem: Amongst three-dimensional Bravais lattices with determinant $1$, which lattice minimises the $p$-th moment of the lattice Voronoi cell? Barnes and Sloane (1983) proved that the BCC lattice is optimal for the case $p=2$, which is known as the vector quantization problem in the signal compression literature. Bambah (1954) proved that the BCC lattice is optimal for the limiting case $p=\infty$, which is the sphere covering problem. Based on these results, Graf and Luschgy (2000) conjectured that the BCC lattice is optimal for all $p \in [1,\infty)$. Three dimensions is the critical dimension in the sense that in two dimensions the optimal lattice is independent of $p$, whereas in four dimensions it varies with $p$. In this paper we give support in favour of Graf and Luschgy's conjecture by proving that the BCC lattice is a local minimiser for all $p \in [1,\infty)$ and a global minimiser for $p$ near 2. While the conjecture asserts that the global minimiser is independent of $p$, we prove a bifurcation theorem which shows that the set of critical points depends on $p$ and that $p=2$ is a distinguished case. Our proofs combine results from discrete geometry by Barnes and Sloane (1983) and Conway and Sloane (1992) with optimal transport theory, the calculus of variations, bifurcation theory, and some delicate positivity estimates.
item.dc:creator: David P. Bourne, Filippo Cagnetti, Steven M. Roper

item.title: Wulff Rigidity for Overdetermined Anisotropic $k$-Hessian Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.39756v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish Wulff rigidity for overdetermined anisotropic $k$-Hessian equations associated with a smooth and strongly convex Finsler gauge. The solutions are subject to homogeneous Dirichlet boundary and a prescribed anisotropic gradient condition on a smooth domain. We prove that the domain must be a Wulff shape. The same rigidity holds under a prescribed positive weighted Neumann-type condition. These results extend the Wulff rigidity for the endpoint cases $k=1$ (Cianchi--Salani, \emph{Math. Ann.}, 2009; Wang--Xia \emph{Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal.}, 2011) and $k=n$ ( Cianchi--Salani, \emph{J. Funct. Anal.}, 2023) to the intermediate cases $2\le k<n$.
item.dc:creator: Lichun Liang, Yanjun Liu

item.title: Arbitrary Dirichlet Eigenvalue Multiplicities on Smooth Star-Shaped Euclidean Domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.39794v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In every fixed dimension \(N\ge3\), for any finite list of positive integers \(m_1,\ldots,m_\ell\), we construct smooth strictly star-shaped Euclidean domains whose first \(\ell+1\) distinct Dirichlet eigenvalues can have multiplicities \(1,m_1,\ldots,m_\ell\) respectively. The condition "star-shaped" is almost optimal in the sense that this statement can not hold for bounded convex domains. In fact, we show that the second Dirichlet eigenvalue of any bounded convex domain has multiplicity at most $N$, and this bound is sharp.
item.dc:creator: Zhijie Chen, Chen-Gang Long, Shihong Zhang

item.title: Euler--Lagrange Flow Monotonicity for the Radon Transform
item.description: arXiv:2610.39818v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a new gradient-like flow that targets critical points of the inequality for the planar Radon transform $\mathcal{R}$ proven by Oberlin and Stein, partially answering a question of Christ, who gave a complete characterisation of the extremisers of the inequality via rearrangement methods. We show that for non-negative radial initial data near the extremiser manifold, solutions to the flow exist globally and there exists a rescaled subsequence of the flow that converges to a critical point of the Radon functional $\|\mathcal{R} f\|_3/\|f\|_{3/2}$ locally in $L^{3/2}(\mathbb{R}^2)$. We also obtain a quantitative result for the rate of decay of critical points, which complements a result of Christ arXiv:1106.0719 in the special case of radial functions. We prove a novel localised smoothing estimate for the operator $\mathcal{R}^*[(\mathcal{R}\cdot)^2]$ restricted to radial functions. This approach is complementary to that of Christ and provides a robust framework for studying extremal problems associated to Radon-like operators.
item.dc:creator: Yannis Galanos

item.title: Klein-Gordon-Born-Infeld equations driven by mixed local-nonlocal operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.39829v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we study a class of Klein-Gordon-Born-Infeld systems in which the classical Laplacian appearing in the matter equation is replaced by a mixed local-nonlocal operator, whose nonlocal part is allowed to be nonpositive definite according to a real parameter. Both the approximate and the exact Born-Infeld field equations are considered in parallel. After making the functional framework explicit, we identify a range of real parameters for which infinitely many radially symmetric standing waves exist, obtained as Mountain Pass critical points of the associated reduced energy functionals. The mixed local-nonlocal operator reduces to the classical Laplacian as the nonlocal weight vanishes, and is motivated, in the spirit of effective field theories, by nonlocal corrections to the matter dispersion relation.
item.dc:creator: Nicol\`o Cangiotti, Maicol Caponi, Alberto Maione, Enzo Vitillaro

item.title: Instability theory of stationary solutions for nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.39830v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the orbital instability of algebraically decaying stationary solutions of nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations in dimensions $d\ge2$, taking competing double-power nonlinearities as a canonical model. At zero frequency, the essential spectrum of the linearized operator touches zero, and the usual $H^1$ coercivity is lost. We construct the zero-frequency limit $\eta_0$ of the frequency derivatives $\partial_\omega\phi_\omega$ of standing-wave profiles and determine its sharp asymptotic behavior. For a stationary ground state $\phi_0\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$, we prove instability if $\langle x\rangle\,\phi_0\notin L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$ or, when $\langle x\rangle\,\phi_0\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$, if the duality pairing $\langle\eta_0,\phi_0\rangle$ is negative. This criterion is a zero-frequency counterpart of the negative slope condition in the Grillakis--Shatah--Strauss theory. The proof combines variation of parameters for the linearized ODE with a shooting analysis that determines the global behavior of the homogeneous solution regular at the origin. We then localize $\eta_0$ to construct an unstable direction and establish instability through a Lyapunov functional argument based on the variational characterization of ground states. The results extend with essentially the same proofs to a class of multiple-power nonlinearities.
item.dc:creator: Noriyoshi Fukaya, Masayuki Hayashi

item.title: Variational characterization of principal eigenvalues for a general class of linear weighted BVP's under mixed boundary conditions of non-classical type
item.description: arXiv:2610.39940v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The main goal of this paper is to characterize the existence of principal eigenvalues of $$ \left \{ \begin{array}{ll} -\mathrm{div}\left(A\nabla u\right) +qu=\lambda m u \quad & \hbox{in} \;\; \Omega,\\[1ex] \mathscr{B} u = 0 \quad & \hbox{on} \;\; \partial \Omega, \end{array} \right. $$ where $m\in L^\infty(\Omega)$ satisfies some of the conditions (A1)-(A3) below, as well as to deliver their variational characterizations whenever they exist. As we are dealing with general boundary operators of mixed non-classical type, in the general setting of this paper our results are far more general than all existing results. The case when $m$ satisfies (A2) has not been previously explored in the literature.
item.dc:creator: Juli\'an L\'opez-G\'omez, Alejandro Sahuquillo

item.title: Sharp regularity for the anisotropic fractional Laplacian with Morrey data
item.description: arXiv:2610.39947v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We obtain sharp regularity for the anisotropic fractional Laplace equation with a right-hand side belonging to a Morrey space. We derive local $C^{\sigma+\lambda-n}-$regularity of solutions when $\sigma+\lambda-n\neq1$, where $\sigma\in(0,2)$ is the order of the operator and $\lambda\in(n-\sigma,n)$ is the Morrey decay rate of the right-hand side. In the case $\sigma+\lambda-n=1$, we show that solutions are locally in the Zygmund class, and hence are Log-Lipschitz continuous. Explicit examples attest to the sharpness of the conditions.
item.dc:creator: Rafayel Teymurazyan, Jos\'e Miguel Urbano

item.title: The H\'enon equation beyond the critical Sobolev exponent
item.description: arXiv:2610.39976v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the Dirichlet problem $-\Delta u=|x|^\alpha u^p$, $u>0$ in $\Omega$, $u=0$ on $\partial\Omega$, where $\Omega\subset R^N$, $N\ge 3$, is a bounded domain containing the origin and $\alpha>0$. We prove that a solution exists for every exponent $1<p<p_\alpha=\frac{N+2+2\alpha}{N-2}$, in particular in the whole Sobolev-supercritical range $\frac{N+2}{N-2}\le p<p_\alpha$, provided $\Omega$ is invariant under $O(N-1)\times O(1)$ and satisfies an angular monotonicity condition. This class contains the balls, the oblate ellipsoids of revolution, lens-shaped domains, and non-convex, non-smooth and non star-shaped domains. The solution is obtained by minimizing the Rayleigh quotient on a suitable closed convex cone.
item.dc:creator: Francesca Gladiali, Massimo Grossi

item.title: A Liouville theorem for plurisubharmonic functions with periodic complex Monge-Amp\`ere measure
item.description: arXiv:2610.40004v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study entire continuous plurisubharmonic solutions of the complex Monge-Amp\`ere equation $(i\partial\bar\partial u)^n=2^n n!\mu$ in $\mathbb{C}^n$, in the Bedford-Taylor sense, where $\mu\not\equiv 0$ is a nonnegative locally finite Borel measure periodic with respect to a lattice of full real rank. We assume that $\mu$ is locally dominated by complex Monge-Amp\`ere measures of H\"older continuous plurisubharmonic functions, a condition under which the existence theorem of Demailly et al. yields H\"older continuous periodic correctors. Under this assumption, we prove that every such solution with positive two-sided quadratic growth can be written uniquely, up to an additive constant, as the sum of a real quadratic polynomial and a H\"older continuous periodic function.
item.dc:creator: Jingchen Hu, Xushan Tu

item.title: A nonlocal transport problem describing pore growth
item.description: arXiv:2610.40019v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a nonlocal transport problem describing pore growth in a biological membrane exposed to a periodic electric potential, where the growth term is modified through the first moment of the solution $n_1(t)$. We show that for initial data $f_0$ with noncompact support it holds $n_1(t) \rightarrow \infty$ , whereas for $f_0$ with compact support the limit of $n_1$ depends sensitively on the data. For a broad class of initial data we additionally obtain $n_1 \sim t^{\frac{1}{2}}$. In the case of a constant external potential we further prove that solutions converge to the self-similar solution having the same tail behaviour as $f_0$.
item.dc:creator: Barbara Niethammer, Lorena Pohl, Juan J. L. Vel\'azquez

item.title: $\gamma$-Valued Stein--Tomas Restriction for Schatten Classes
item.description: arXiv:2610.40044v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\Sigma\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a compact $C^2$ hypersurface with nonvanishing Gaussian curvature. We prove the sharp matrix-dimension-independent Schatten-valued Stein--Tomas range \[ R_\Sigma:L^p(\mathbb R^3;S^a)\longrightarrow\gamma(L^2(\Sigma),S^a), \qquad 1<a<\infty,\quad 1\le p\le\min\{a,4/3\}. \] The core endpoint is $E_\Sigma:\gamma(L^2(\Sigma),S^4)\to L^4(\mathbb R^3;S^4)$. After squaring the quartic norm, multiplication lands in the Hilbert--Schmidt class. A local coarea argument splits resonant quartets according to the shorter adjacent frequency chord, producing a dimension-free row/column estimate for elliptic and hyperbolic curvature. We also show that Gaussian type $4/3$ alone does not characterize the corresponding endpoint for arbitrary Banach spaces. Applications include matrix Herglotz waves, a two-dimensional Schr\"odinger $L^4$ estimate, and free spectral-measure bounds.
item.dc:creator: R. Shahmurov, V. Shahmurov

item.title: Local $Tb$ theorems in non-homogeneous metric spaces, and applications to caloric measure
item.description: arXiv:2610.40135v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a local $Tb$ theorem with testing conditions on metric balls, for possibly non-doubling measures of polynomial growth on geometrically doubling metric spaces. It resolves the maximal-truncation version of Hofmann's local $Tb$ problem for all $1<p,q\leq\infty$, without assuming antisymmetry of the Calder\'on-Zygmund kernel. Our theorem allows accretive systems of complex testing measures satisfying a quantitative small-set condition; these measures need not be absolutely continuous with respect to the underlying measure. Testing requires only a one-level $L^0$ bound for maximal truncations, with an alternative for balls on which the underlying measure concentrates in a set of small relative diameter. We also remove antisymmetry from the known buffered and unbuffered fixed-truncation criteria. The proof combines a mixed corona decomposition adapted to the two testing systems with two-measure $L^2$ estimates for suppressed operators. As an application in the parabolic space $\mathbb P^n$, local time-directed $A_\infty$-type conditions on caloric and adjoint caloric measure imply $L^2(\sigma)$-boundedness of the spatial gradient of the heat single layer potential for boundary measures $\sigma$ with upper parabolic $(n+1)$-growth. This gives a parabolic counterpart of the harmonic-measure theorem of Mourgoglou and Tolsa without Ahlfors regularity, corkscrew or Harnack chain assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Merlo, Mihalis Mourgoglou, Carmelo Puliatti

item.title: The fractional Faber--Krahn inequality in sharp quantitative form
item.description: arXiv:2610.40232v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of the fractional Laplacian satisfies the sharp quantitative Faber--Krahn inequality. This was conjectured by Brasco, Cinti and Vita, who proved the inequality with a sub-optimal exponent. The proof adapts to the non-local setting the level-set argument recently introduced by Guerra, Machado and Ramos for the Laplacian. It is carried out on the horizontal level sets of the Caffarelli--Silvestre extension of the torsion function, where the asymmetry appears only as a boundary value at the corner of the extension variables.
item.dc:creator: Michael Goldman, Matteo Novaga, Berardo Ruffini

item.title: Second variation of the fractional torsion energy and linear stability of the ball
item.description: arXiv:2610.40240v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute the second shape derivative of the fractional torsion. It is an explicit quadratic form on the boundary, which involves a Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator for half-harmonic functions blowing up at the boundary. We deduce an explicit formula for volume preserving variations on the ball and show that as in the local case, the shape Hessian is negative and coercive in \(H^{1/2}\) modulo translations.
item.dc:creator: Michael Goldman, Matteo Novaga, Berardo Ruffini

item.title: Drift-diffusion equations with saturation on $\mathbb{R}^d$
item.description: arXiv:2610.40294v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a class of nonlinear drift--diffusion equations on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with saturation-type mobilities, not necessarily concave. Under structural assumptions on the mobility and potentials, bounded-domain approximations and local Caccioppoli estimates yield weak solutions for all positive times and an $L^1$-contraction estimate. The same estimates provide local space--time compactness of time translates, whose subsequential limits are weak solutions. Under additional confinement assumptions, uniform mass-tail estimates yield a mass-preserving, free-energy dissipating $C_0$-semigroup of $L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$-contractions. In this confining setting, every trajectory converges strongly in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$ to a stationary state with the same mass, and the resulting time-limit operator is an $L^1$-contraction. Under the same assumptions, we also identify the unique global and $L^1$-local minimiser of the free energy at each fixed mass and prove that it is stationary under the semigroup.
item.dc:creator: Alejandro Fern\'andez-Jim\'enez

item.title: Nonuniqueness and failure of positivity preservation for doubly critical semilinear heat equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.40315v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: At the Fujita exponent $p=1+2/N$ we construct a strictly positive mild solution of $u_t-\Delta u=|u|^{p-1}u$ in $\mathbb R^N$ whose initial trace in $L^1$ is zero. In similarity variables the solution approaches a Gaussian profile, and $$\|U(t)\|_1\sim C_N(\log(1/t))^{-N/2},\qquad \|U(t)\|_\infty\sim c_Nt^{-N/2}(\log(1/t))^{-N/2},$$ with explicit constants $C_N$ and $c_N$. In particular, uniqueness fails at the borderline logarithmic rate, and the solution lies outside every stronger logarithmic uniqueness class; this answers two questions raised by Miyamoto [J. Evol. Equ. 21 (2021), 151--166, Remark~1.6]. We also prove that, up to time translation, this is the only ancient solution of fixed sign of the rescaled equation that decays in a Gaussian weighted supremum norm. On a bounded smooth domain the whole-space solution can be localized at finitely many interior points, with independently chosen signs, on top of an arbitrary bounded initial datum. The resulting solutions are classical for $t>0$ and continuous at $t=0$ in $L^1$. Consequently, uniqueness fails for every bounded datum, and positivity is lost for every bounded nonnegative datum, $u_0\equiv1$ included. These results provide affirmative answers to Open Problems~3 and~4 posed by Brezis and Cazenave in [J. Anal. Math. 68 (1996), 277--304].
item.dc:creator: Berikbol T. Torebek

item.title: Relativistic collision geometry and global near-vacuum solutions at critical transverse regularity
item.description: arXiv:2610.40322v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish global well-posedness near vacuum for the relativistic Boltzmann equation with soft and hard potentials in the range $\gamma\in(-2,1]$. The initial data have critical Besov regularity of order $2/r$ in the transverse spatial variables for an admissible range of $r$ depending on $\gamma$, together with weighted integrability in the longitudinal and momentum variables. The proof combines a fixed-direction div--curl lemma with bilinear collision estimates. In particular, to control the gain term, we combine localization to spherical caps with energy-weighted angular estimates. The key relativistic estimate controls the singularity associated with the first component of the post-collisional relative velocity. These bounds yield the required time decay.
item.dc:creator: Xinfeng Hu, Shuangqian Liu, Haoran Peng, Yi Zhou

item.title: Stationary Structures of the Boussinesq equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.40334v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the steady configurations supported by the inviscid two-dimensional Boussinesq equations in the periodic channel. We show steady laminar velocity fields (closed non-contractible fluid trajectories) coupled to non-decreasing density stratifications are necessarily stratified shear flows. The direction of density monotonicity along level sets is in fact fundamental: in striking contrast with the Euler equations, we exhibit laminar non-stagnant non-shear stationary solutions in the periodic channel. We also provide distinct flexibility and rigidity results (laminar persistence or appearance of islands for nearby non-shear solutions) close to stratified shear flows according to their stagnation points. As a by-product of our analysis, we establish a uniform Crandall-Rabinowitz bifurcation theorem that might be of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Marc Nualart, Jaemin Park, Javier Pe\~nafiel-Tom\'as

item.title: Sharp $L^2$ stability for anisotropic radial Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2610.40360v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish quantitative stability for radial Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequalities involving the anisotropic radial derivative and the Minkowski functional of a smooth, strictly convex body in $\mathbb R^N$, $N\ge2$. Here, the convex body need not be origin-symmetric. For the $L^2$-Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequality, we establish the sharp stability constant $|b+1-a|$ for $a\ne b+1$, and classify all equality cases in the natural weighted completion spaces, by optimizing over the angular coefficients and a common dilation parameter. We also obtain the sharp stability constants $2$ and $4$ for the scale-invariant and scale-noninvariant $L^2$-Heisenberg inequality, respectively. For $2\le p<\infty$, we also establish weighted stability of the anisotropic radial $L^p$-Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequalities when $a\neq b+1$ and $(b+1-a)(N-p(b+1))\geq0$, and the anisotropic radial $L^p$-Heisenberg inequalities. As a byproduct, we establish weighted $L^p$-Poincar\'e inequalities for Gamma measures, which serve as the main tool for our stability estimates.
item.dc:creator: Zhenzhen Wei, Denghui Wu

item.title: Quantitative propagation of chaos on arbitrary finite time intervals for the three-dimensional repulsive Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.40422v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove quantitative propagation of chaos in total variation for repulsive Vlasov--Riesz--Fokker--Planck (VRFP) equations on $\mathbb{T}^d$ and $\mathbb{R}^d$ with unregularized interaction potentials with singularity $|x|^{-s}$, $0<s<d/2$. On every finite time interval on which the limiting classical solution satisfies the stated regularity assumptions, the particle marginals with a product initial law converge at an algebraic rate in the particle number, with constants growing at most exponentially in the marginal order. For the three-dimensional repulsive Vlasov--Poisson--Fokker--Planck (VPFP) equation on $\mathbb{R}^3$, a weighted $C^m$ initial probability density, $m\ge3$, with Gaussian velocity decay and polynomial spatial decay of order $M>3$ gives convergence to the global classical solution on every finite time interval. The proof combines conditioning of the initial product law with weighted BBGKY estimates. A decomposition of the potential and a bounded modification of the far-field force yield weighted bounds growing geometrically in the marginal order on the prescribed interval. A centered second-moment estimate permits summation of the error hierarchy, and a synchronous coupling transfers the estimate to the original dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Ning Jiang, Juntao Wu

item.title: An alternative proof of the Keel--Tao endpoint Strichartz estimates
item.description: arXiv:2610.40434v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we give an alternative proof of the abstract endpoint Strichartz estimates proved by Keel and Tao. Our method is based on the near-far decomposition technique, which was developed in a recent work by Toyoshima and the author.
item.dc:creator: Sonae Hadama

item.title: On the existence of minimizers for the generalized liquid drop model
item.description: arXiv:2610.40500v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a broad class of generalized liquid drop models in which a perimeter term competes with repulsive nonlocal interactions with finite first moments. For all such kernels satisfying the natural physical assumption of reflection positivity we show existence of minimizers for all masses, in the (super-)critical regime. Moreover, in the subcritical regime we give the first quantitative estimate of the range of masses for which existence holds, which converges to the whole positive real line as one approaches the critical regime. This result builds on the nonlocal curvature approach introduced and developed in the periodic setting in \cite{dr24}.
item.dc:creator: Xiaopeng Cheng, Sara Daneri, Eris Runa

item.title: Global Well-Posedness of Landau Equation in Bounded Domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.40517v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove global well-posedness of the Landau equation near a Maxwellian in bounded $C^3$ domains with in-flow or diffuse-reflection boundary conditions for $-3\leq\gamma\leq1$, including Coulomb interactions. Small compatible Gaussian perturbations generate global strong solutions, with uniqueness and continuous dependence among weak solutions. The proof combines energy estimates, the comparison principle, interior and weighted boundary estimates for velocity derivatives up to second order, and a logarithmic estimate for solution difference.
item.dc:creator: Zhimeng Ouyang, Lei Wu

item.title: Sharp lifespan estimates for heat equations with H\"ormander operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.40547v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the Cauchy problem $u_t-\mathcal L u=h(t)u^p$, $u(0)=\varepsilon u_0\ge0$, where $p>1$, $h\ge0$ is only locally integrable, and $\mathcal L=\sum_{j=1}^mX_j^2$ is a homogeneous H\"ormander sum of squares on $\mathbb R^n$ of homogeneous dimension $q$. Diffusion spreads the solution out and weakens the nonlinearity, while the reaction $h(t)u^p$ may force blow-up. We prove that the outcome is decided by the single quantity $\mathcal{H}_{p,h}(T)=\int_0^Th(t)(1+t)^{-\frac q2(p-1)}\,d t$, in which the reaction at time $t$ is weighted by the factor by which diffusion has weakened the solution: small data are global if $\mathcal{H}_{p,h}(\infty)<\infty$, while otherwise the lifespan $T_\varepsilon$ satisfies $c\,\varepsilon^{-(p-1)}\le\mathcal{H}_{p,h}(T_\varepsilon)\le C\,\varepsilon^{-(p-1)}$ for small $\varepsilon$. Our technique of proof is based on a backward-semigroup functional combined with a Gaussian-envelope energy and an ODE cap telescoped along interlaced geometric grids. The result contains the Euclidean, Heisenberg, Carnot and Grushin cases, yields explicit lifespan laws for power, logarithmic, exponential, periodic and intermittent coefficients, and exhibits effects with no autonomous counterpart, such as a lifespan with no power law in $\varepsilon$. We also prove regularity and a priori estimates for classical solutions and discuss what remains true for a general nonlinearity $f(u)$.
item.dc:creator: Michael Ruzhansky, Berikbol T. Torebek

item.title: A Sharp Uniqueness-Nonuniqueness Dichotomy for Neutral Vortex Arrays in $2$D Euler Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.40552v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a sharp uniqueness--nonuniqueness criterion for the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equations within a class of stationary arrays of disjoint neutral vortices. Let $\Theta$ be any finite nondecreasing envelope for the vorticity $L^p$ norms, and set $I_\Theta=\int_{p_0}^\infty \Theta(p)^{-1}\,dp$. If $I_\Theta=\infty$, every array in the corresponding class admits a unique Euler evolution, even among bounded energy-admissible weak velocity solutions. If $I_\Theta<\infty$, there exists a compactly supported array in the same class admitting two distinct unforced Lagrangian Euler evolutions from the same initial datum. The criterion holds for arbitrary nondecreasing envelopes $\Theta$.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Y. Hou, Xiang Qin, Peicong Song, Wenhan Zhang

item.title: Nonuniqueness of the $2$D Euler Evolutions with $L^1\cap L^p$ Vorticity
item.description: arXiv:2610.40553v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For each prescribed $1<p<\infty$, we construct a compactly supported initial vorticity in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)\cap L^p(\mathbb{R}^2)$ that admits two distinct evolutions under the unforced two-dimensional incompressible Euler equation on $[0,1]$. Both vorticities are strongly continuous in $L^1\cap L^p$ and are transported exactly by their respective almost-everywhere invertible, measure-preserving regular Lagrangian flows. The construction couples unstable four-vortex configurations across increasingly small spatial scales, realizing them through concentrated signed vortex patches. At each finite cutoff, a prepared reference evolution remains close to rotating configurations, while a second evolution differs initially only at the finest scale. In the second evolution, the finest configuration consists of separating dipoles whose remote strain activates the instability of the next larger configuration. This process propagates through successive scales with summable transition times. As the cutoff tends to infinity, the two families of initial data converge strongly, along a subsequence, to the same datum, while a nonzero difference survives at a fixed larger scale and is detected by a fixed smooth observable at a positive limiting time. Quantitative concentration and relative comparison estimates establish this cascade for exact Euler patch solutions. Strong compactness through inverse-flow stability then preserves both exact vorticity transport and the positive-time distinction between the two limiting evolutions. The initial datum and construction parameters may depend on $p$.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Y. Hou, Xiang Qin, Peicong Song, Wenhan Zhang

item.title: Critical Robin Problems on Manifolds with Noncompact Boundary
item.description: arXiv:2610.40603v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We work on connected, noncompact $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifolds $(\mathcal{M}, g), n \geq 3$, that are complete with respect to $d_g$ and have noncompact boundary and bounded geometry. We study the existence of positive solutions in $C^{\infty}(\mathcal{M}) \cap L^{2^*}(\mathcal{M}) \cap L^{\infty}(\mathcal{M})$ to the Yamabe problem: $$ \left\{\begin{aligned} -\Delta_g u+\frac{n-2}{4(n-1)} R_g u & =\mathscr{C}_0 u^{\frac{n+2}{n-2}} \quad \text { in } \mathcal{M}, \\ \frac{\partial u}{\partial \nu}+\frac{n-2}{2(n-1)} H_g u & =\mathscr{C}_1 u^{\frac{n}{n-2}} \quad \text { on } \partial \mathcal{M}, \end{aligned}\right. $$ where $\mathscr{C}_0=Y_{\mathscr{C}}(\mathcal{M}), \mathscr{C}_1=Y_{\mathscr{C}}(\mathcal{M}) \mathscr{C} \bar{d}^{\frac{2}{n-2}}$, the parameter $\mathscr{C} \geq 0$ is fixed, and $$ Y_{\mathscr{C}}(\mathcal{M}):=\inf _{u \in C_c^{\infty}(\mathcal{M}) \backslash\{0\}} \frac{E_g(u)}{\left(\|u\|_{L^{2^*}(\mathcal{M})}^{2^*}+\mathscr{C}\|u\|_{L^{2^{\#}}(\partial \mathcal{M})}^{2^*}\right)^{2 / 2^*}} . $$ Here $E_g$ is the associated quadratic energy. We assume $Y_{\mathscr{C}}(\mathcal{M})<Y_{\mathscr{C}, \infty}(\mathcal{M})$ and $Y_{\mathscr{C}, \infty}(\mathcal{M})>0$, where $Y_{\mathscr{C}, \infty}$ is the corresponding variational level at infinity. We approach this problem using nonnegative solutions $u_j \in W_{\partial}^{1,2}\left(B_g(\mathcal{O}, j)\right), j \in \mathbb{N}, j \geq j_0$, for which we prove that $$ \sup _{j \geq j_0}\left\|u_j\right\|_{L^{\infty}\left(B_g(\mathcal{O}, j-1)\right)}<\infty . $$ For $\mathscr{C}>0$, we also prove that, along a subsequence, $\left\|u_j\right\|_{L^2{ }_{\left(B_g(\mathcal{O}, j) \cap \partial \mathcal{M}\right)}} \rightarrow \bar{d}$, with $0<\bar{d} \leq \mathscr{C}^{-1 / 2^*}$. For $\mathscr{C}=0$, we set $\bar{d}=0$.
item.dc:creator: Juan Pablo Alcon Apaza

item.title: The generalized Cartan-Hadamard conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.37817v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish the generalized Cartan-Hadamard conjecture, including rigidity in the equality case. As a corollary, we obtain that isoperimetric regions are bounded. We prove the conjecture for Alexandrov spaces with two sided curvature bounds as well. A sharp Michael-Simon-type inequality for hypersurfaces in these spaces is also shown.
item.dc:creator: Marcos Agnoletto, M\'arcio Fabiano Da Silva, Stefano Nardulli, Reinaldo Resende

item.title: Regularizing the Navier-Stokes Equations via Additive Type Noise plus Small Linear Multiplicative Noise
item.description: arXiv:2610.38018v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We derive a series of ``regularization by noise in high probability" results for incompressible Navier-Stokes equations $(d\geq3)$, via a new mechanism based on fixed point argument: For initial values in critical Besov space $\dot{B}_{q,\infty}^{-1+d/q}~ (1\leq q<\infty)$, we can expect unique global solutions with $C_{w^*,loc}\big([0,\infty);\dot{B}_{q,\infty}^{-1+d/q}\big)$-paths in high probability if the equations are perturbed by well-constructed additive type noise; for initial values in the ``end-point space" $\dot{B}_{\infty,\infty}^{-1}$ where the equations are locally ill-posed in deterministic setting \cite{BP08}, we can still expect unique solutions on $[0,T]$ (with ``modified" $*$-weak continuous paths) in high probability for large enough $T>0$, if the equations are perturbed by a well-constructed additive type noise plus a ``small" linear multiplicative noise. This means that the regularizing effect can be strengthen by small additional linear multiplicative noise in the sense that the Picard iteration remains effective for values in the largest critical space $\dot{B}_{\infty,\infty}^{-1}$. This work has nothing to do with AI models.
item.dc:creator: Weiquan Chen

item.title: Neural Stream Function Method for Electrical Impedance Tomography with Lipschitz Conductivities
item.description: arXiv:2610.38064v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Electrical impedance tomography (EIT) reconstructs the conductivity inside an object from voltage and current measurements on its boundary. The resulting inverse problem is nonlinear and severely ill-posed. Neural networks offer a flexible computational approach, but training physics informed neural networks for EIT and relating their training loss to reconstruction accuracy remain challenging. We develop a novel constrained neural stream function method for planar EIT with Lipschitz conductivities. The method builds the conductivity constraints and prescribed boundary voltages into the neural trial functions and replaces the second order conductivity equation with a first order system in strong form. The measured current is also used to construct a fixed baseline for the stream function. For this formulation, we derive error estimates that relate the sampled neural objective to errors in the physical boundary currents and the reconstructed conductivity. The error estimates separate the contributions from neural approximation, measurement noise, and sampling. Numerical experiments further demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high reconstruction accuracy with both exact and noisy boundary data.
item.dc:creator: Xiaosheng Li

item.title: Notes on Orlicz Spaces and Interpolation
item.description: arXiv:2610.38455v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Orlicz spaces are a natural generalization of classical Lebesgue spaces. They are built upon convex growth functions and provide a flexible framework for studying integrability conditions beyond power-type behavior. In this survey paper, we present the basic definitions, main properties, and fundamental results concerning Orlicz spaces, and also discuss the Marcinkiewicz interpolation result for Orlicz spaces.
item.dc:creator: M. Vali Siadat, Wilfredo Urbina-Romero

item.title: The General-Relativistic Limit of f(R) Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2610.38795v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish the general-relativistic limit of f(R) gravity coupled to a massless scalar field for small, asymptotically Euclidean, well-prepared Cauchy data near Minkowski spacetime. We prove global existence and future causal geodesic completeness, with uniform estimates for the metric, matter, and rescaled effective field as an admissible family of modified Lagrangians f(R) approaches the Einstein-Hilbert Lagrangian R. The physical and conformal metrics and the matter field converge to the limiting Einstein-massless-scalar development, uniformly on the entire future spacetime, together with finitely many space and time derivatives. The effective field, defined by a nonlinear reparametrization of the physical scalar curvature, converges to the scalar curvature of the limiting Einstein development. The main analytical difficulty is that the effective-field mass tends to infinity, while its evolution equation becomes an algebraic trace relation. Small field amplitudes may coexist with high-frequency oscillations and comparatively large derivatives, whose quadratic contributions must be controlled uniformly. Using the Euclidean-hyperboloidal foliation method and adapted wave coordinates, we analyze a quasilinear wave-Klein-Gordon system whose nonlinearities do not satisfy the classical null condition. We combine oscillatory estimates, weighted interior and exterior energies, and propagation estimates for the discrepancy from the Einstein trace relation. Quantitative convergence on compact regions and uniform spacetime decay yield global convergence.
item.dc:creator: Philippe G. LeFloch, Yue Ma

item.title: Mean-convex horizontal mean curvature flow in the Heisenberg group
item.description: arXiv:2610.38929v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the arrival time equation of the mean-convex horizontal mean curvature flow in the Heisenberg group. We prove existence of viscosity solutions when the initial set is horizontally mean-convex and either non-characteristic, or axisymmetric and with horizontal mean curvature extending continuously across the characteristic set. A key ingredient is an approximation scheme by sets with prescribed Riemannian mean curvature, which preserves the mean-curvature bounds up to an arbitrarily small error. We further show that, when the evolving level sets form a generalized \(C^2\)-foliation, the horizontal mean curvature blows up around characteristic points. This provides an obstruction to self-similar evolution in the axisymmetric class considered above and, in particular, shows that the Pansu sphere cannot evolve self-similarly.
item.dc:creator: Gaia Bombardieri, Mattia Fogagnolo, Valentina Franceschi

item.title: Minimally-coupled Quasilinear Symmetric Hyperbolic Systems, Naturally
item.description: arXiv:2610.39107v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider symmetric hyperbolicity and well-posedness in the context of natural equations, which are closed subobjects of jet bundles over natural bundles. We show how non-natural equations can be "naturalized", and we discuss how a precise version of "minimal coupling" offers a (provably unique, up to isomorphism) method for constructing natural equations from certain equations defined on a single manifold. We discuss how to define symmetrizers, hyperbolizations, and constraints for minimally coupled natural equations, and we show how these can be used to recover standard existence and uniqueness results, relative to any choice of background structure (a metric, for minimally coupled systems). Additionally, we show that minimal coupling and naturality together imply that the causal cones associated with a (first order, quasilinear, minimally coupled) naturally symmetric hyperbolic natural equation must always coincide with the metric lightcones, and that a certain rank-2 tensor, associates with a natural hyperbolization, must always be divergence free relative to the associated Levi-Civita derivative operator.
item.dc:creator: Eleanor March, James Owen Weatherall

item.title: The seeds and silhouettes of optimal gravitational shielding
item.description: arXiv:2610.39262v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct complete vacuum initial data sets with prescribed asymptotically flat exterior geometry, including the gluing of two Schwarzschild exterior regions with small masses (which need not be positive). The construction allows for arbitrarily slow leading decay and nonzero second fundamental form. For leading terms with a fixed radial power, we first construct localized seed data sets whose constraint errors decay to any prescribed finite order, then apply the projection and stability theorems of our companion papers. The resulting vacuum data sets differ from seeds by harmonic terms controlled by Hamiltonian and momentum silhouettes, and by super-harmonic corrections. This difference of harmonic terms is measured by a relative notion of ADM energy-momentum, which is defined even for slowly-decaying data sets that do not admit an ADM energy-momentum. Upon adjusting seed data sets by either harmonic-decaying terms or compact transverse-traceless terms, we freely control this relative ADM charge and, when it exists, the total ADM charge. In particular, when gluing Schwarzschild metrics the total ADM mass can be specified independently of the Schwarzschild mass parameters. Together with our companion papers, these results establish a constructive theory of optimal localization beyond harmonic decay.
item.dc:creator: Bruno Le Floch, Philippe G. LeFloch

item.title: Existence and spectral instability of steady rolls in the Nikolaevskiy equation: a computer-assisted study
item.description: arXiv:2610.39611v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Nikolaevskiy equation is a model of short-wave pattern formation coupled to a neutral long-wave mode, and it is believed that all of its spatially periodic steady states are unstable. Existing results are formal, numerical, or restricted to a small neighbourhood of onset. We give computer-assisted proofs of three results. First, for every wavenumber q in [0.9, 1.1] and every control parameter r between the onset value (1-q^2)^2 and 4, the equation has a nontrivial, real-analytic, odd steady roll; these rolls form a single continuous two-parameter family that bifurcates from the trivial state at onset, with an explicit amplitude bound proportional to the square root of the distance to onset. Second, every roll of this family with r in [0.25, 4] is spectrally unstable on the real line: its linearisation has a Bloch eigenvalue with real part at least 6.7e-4, and at least 0.13 for r >= 0.575. Third, at nine sample points we enclose, at a small Bloch number, the eigenvalue numerically identified with the long-wave (Matthews-Cox) branch; its real part is positive at seven points and negative at two, while strongly unstable eigenvalues exist at all nine. The proofs combine a parametrised Newton-Kantorovich theorem, a desingularisation near onset, Taylor-model bounds on parameter boxes, and a Weyl-sequence argument for the Bloch spectrum; all estimates are evaluated in rigorous interval arithmetic.
item.dc:creator: Nikita V. Konev, Fedor A. Vyazanitsyn, Igor A. Knyazev

item.title: A Transfer Principle for Elliptic Carleman Estimates: Application to Discrete Calder\'on Stability
item.description: arXiv:2610.39750v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a transfer principle that lifts continuous elliptic Carleman estimates to mesh-uniform estimates for conforming Galerkin discretizations. The main difficulties are twofold: discrete states generally lack the \(H^2\)-regularity required by the continuous estimate, and the Carleman parameter \(s\) must be controlled relative to the mesh size \(h\). We overcome both by introducing a shifted continuous problem whose Galerkin solution is exactly the conforming reconstruction of a prescribed discrete state. Weighted approximation then transfers the inequality back to the original discrete operator without adding stabilization, and yields the range \(s\le ch^{-4/5}\) for radial weights. We verify the framework for piecewise affine finite elements with consistent or lumped mass on fitted, uniformly shape-regular meshes, and for standard Cartesian finite differences through their finite-element realization. As an application, we study the discrete Calder\'on problem for bounded complex Schr\"odinger potentials in dimension \(d\ge3\). Assuming agreement in a fixed connected boundary neighborhood and uniform stability of the discrete Dirichlet problems, we obtain stability from Dirichlet inputs and variational flux observations on independently prescribed, possibly disjoint boundary patches. The resulting estimate in \(H^{-r}\), \(r>d/2\), retains the single logarithmic data term and the \(O(h^{1/2})\) mesh remainder of the full-data estimate.
item.dc:creator: Qi L\"u, Yu Wang

item.title: A Semigroup-Aware Kernel Neural Operator with Latent Exponential Integration for Forced PDEs
item.description: arXiv:2610.39845v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a semigroup-aware structured kernel neural operator for source-driven evolution PDEs. Unlike generic time-conditioned kernel models, the proposed formulation represents temporal dependence through a latent exponential propagator \(e^{tA_\theta}\), where \(A_\theta\) is a learned latent generator. This provides a structured transition from a non-ODE kernel representation to an ODE-inspired kernel operator whose latent temporal evolution satisfies the composition principle of evolution semigroups. For time-dependent forcing terms, a direct kernel-based evaluation requires repeated quadrature over delayed kernel evaluations. To address this computational bottleneck, we derive a latent-first reformulation of the source term: the forcing field is projected onto the kernel-induced latent space, where its accumulated effect is represented as the solution of a forced linear latent dynamical system. For a fixed learned kernel, this reformulation is exact. The resulting system can then be integrated using a \(\phi_1\)-based exponential integrator, yielding a source-evaluation path that is structurally aligned with the learned latent propagator. The resulting framework combines geometry- and physics-conditioned low-rank kernel factorization with alternative source-evaluation paths based on either explicit Duhamel quadrature or latent exponential integration. Dissipativity constraints on the latent generator and identity-preserving corrections near the initial time are optional architectural components. Numerical experiments on advection-iffusion-reaction (ADR) problems compare the non-ODE and semigroup-aware formulations, evaluate the quadrature and \(\phi_1\) source paths, and assess predictive accuracy and computational cost.
item.dc:creator: Naseem Abbas, Vittorio Colao, Davide Macr\`i, Matthieu Barreau, William Spataro

item.title: A Riemann-Hilbert approach to the two-component modified Camassa-Holm system with step-like boundary conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.39938v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a Riemann--Hilbert formalism for the Cauchy problem for the two-component modified Camassa--Holm (2-mCH) system on the real line under non-zero step-like boundary conditions. Starting from the corresponding Lax pair, we carry out the direct spectral analysis and establish the analytic, symmetry, and asymptotic properties of the eigenfunctions and spectral data determined by the initial conditions. These results are then used to formulate a matrix Riemann--Hilbert problem whose solution provides a reconstruction formula for the solution of the original Cauchy problem.
item.dc:creator: Iryna Karpenko, Dmitry Shepelsky, Gerald Teschl

item.title: Topological defect trains excited by a boundary discontinuity in the two-dimensional complex Ginzburg-Landau equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.40103v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: With numerical simulations of the complex Ginzburg-Landau equation in a two-dimensional space, we find that a stationary but non-zero Dirichlet boundary condition with a discontinuity can drive a periodic train of evenly spaced topological defects that drift along and in proximity to the boundary.
item.dc:creator: Alice C. Quillen, Laura Quinonez

item.title: Monotonicity, continuity and differentiability results for the $L^p$ Hardy constant
item.description: arXiv:1509.09107v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the $L^p$ Hardy inequality involving the distance to the boundary for a domain in the $n$-dimensional Euclidean space. We study the dependence on $p$ of the corresponding best constant and we prove monotonicity, continuity and differentiability results. The focus is on non-convex domains in which case such constant is in general not explicitly known.
item.dc:creator: Gerassimos Barbatis, Pier Domenico Lamberti

item.title: Linear stability analysis for 2D shear flows near Couette in the isentropic Compressible Euler equations
item.description: arXiv:2003.01694v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we investigate linear stability properties of the 2D isentropic compressible Euler equations linearized around a shear flow given by a monotone profile, close to the Couette flow, with constant density, in the domain $\mathbb{T}\times \mathbb{R}$. We begin by directly investigating the Couette shear flow, where we characterize the linear growth of the compressible part of the fluid while proving time decay for the incompressible part (inviscid damping with slower rates). Then we extend the analysis to monotone shear flows near Couette, where we are able to give an upper bound, superlinear in time, for the compressible part of the fluid. The incompressible part enjoys an inviscid damping property, analogous to the Couette case. In the pure Couette case, we exploit the presence of an additional conservation law (which connects the vorticity and the density on the moving frame) in order to reduce the number of degrees of freedom of the system. The result then follows by using weighted energy estimates. In the general case, unfortunately, this conservation law no longer holds. Therefore we define a suitable weighted energy functional for the whole system, which can be used to estimate the irrotational component of the velocity but does not provide sharp bounds on the solenoidal component. However, even in the absence of the aforementioned additional conservation law, we are still able to show the existence of a functional relation which allows us to recover somehow the vorticity from the density, on the moving frame. By combining the weighted energy estimates with the functional relation we also recover the inviscid damping for the solenoidal component of the velocity.
item.dc:creator: Paolo Antonelli, Michele Dolce, Pierangelo Marcati

item.title: $L^p$-theory for the exterior Stokes problem with Navier's type slip-without-friction boundary conditions
item.description: arXiv:2111.05822v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we consider the stationary Stokes equations in an exterior domain three-dimensional under a slip boundary condition without friction. We set the problem in weighted Sobolev spaces in order to control the behavior at infinity of the solutions. In this work, we try to investigate the existence and uniqueness up to an element of a nontrivial kernel of the weak solutions related to this problem in $L^p-$theory when $p>3$. Our proofs are based on obtaining inf-sup conditions that play a fundamental role.
item.dc:creator: Anis Dhifaoui

item.title: Existence and local asymptotics for a system of cross-diffusion equations with nonlocal Cahn-Hilliard terms
item.description: arXiv:2408.07396v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a nonlocal Cahn-Hilliard model for a multicomponent mixture with cross-diffusion effects and degenerate mobility. The nonlocality is described by means of a symmetric singular kernel. We define a notion of weak solution adapted to possible degeneracies and prove, as our first main result, its global-in-time existence. The proof relies on an application of the formal gradient flow structure of the system (to overcome the lack of a priori estimates), combined with an extension of the boundedness-by-entropy method, involving a careful analysis of an auxiliary variational problem. This allows to obtain solutions to an approximate, time-discrete system. Letting the time step size go to zero, we recover the desired nonlocal weak solution where, due to their low regularity, the Cahn-Hilliard terms require a special treatment. Finally, we prove convergence of solutions for this class of nonlocal Cahn-Hilliard equations to their local counterparts.
item.dc:creator: Elisa Davoli, Greta Marino, Jan-Frederik Pietschmann, Nicola Zamponi

item.title: Homogenisation of elasto-plastic evolutions driven by the flow of dislocations
item.description: arXiv:2410.02906v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work establishes the existence of rate-independent elastoplastic evolutions driven by dislocation fields in single crystals via a homogenisation procedure. We use the theory of space-time currents to place the Small-Distortion Geometric Model of [arXiv:2609.23728] on a rigorous footing and conduct the homogenisation by using recently developed normal-to-integral strict approximation results for space-time currents which respect the inherent space-time structure. We prove both a homogenisation and recovery result and thus demonstrate that the field version of the Small-Distortion Geometric Model is well-justified from microscopic principles.
item.dc:creator: Paolo Bonicatto, Filip Rindler, Harry Turnbull

item.title: The evolution equation and the eigenvalue problem for the Laplacian in a regular tree
item.description: arXiv:2506.13728v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, our main goal is to study the evolution problem associated with the Laplacian operator with Dirichlet boundary conditions on a regular tree. To this end, we place special emphasis on the associated first eigenvalue problem, which provides the fundamental tool for describing the long-time dynamics. First, we prove existence and uniqueness of solutions when the initial condition is compatible with the boundary condition. Next, we address the asymptotic behavior of the solutions and show that they decay to zero exponentially fast. This decay rate is determined by the associated first eigenvalue, which we also analyze in detail.
item.dc:creator: Leandro M. Del Pezzo, Nicolas Frevenza, Julio D. Rossi

item.title: Invariant Densities on Cylinders with an Interface: Existence, Uniqueness, and Exponential Asymptotics
item.description: arXiv:2507.15536v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the stationary double-divergence equation on the infinite cylinder $\mathbb R\times\mathbb T^{d-1}$, whose coefficients coincide with two possibly different periodic media outside a bounded interface layer. Under the centering conditions for the two periodic media, we construct a positive invariant density that converges exponentially in $C^1$ at each end to a positive multiple of the corresponding periodic invariant density. Every bounded distributional solution is a scalar multiple of this density. The two asymptotic amplitudes are determined by the full interface problem, up to a common normalization. Motivated by the invariant-measure analysis of Hairer and Manson [Ann. Probab. 39(2011) 648-682], our proof uses only PDE methods: a transformation based on the periodic invariant densities, adjoint Neumann problems on finite cylinders, and energy estimates.
item.dc:creator: Pengxiu Yu, Yiping Zhang

item.title: Joint inviscid, incompressible, and continuous phenotype limit in nonlocal models of tissue growth
item.description: arXiv:2509.16416v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider a multispecies Brinkman tissue-growth system proposed by Debiec, Mandal, and Schmidtchen [J. Differential Equations 2025]. This system adopts a power pressure law determined by the total spatial density and models the effect of phenotype-dependent growth rates on the density dynamics of cells with different phenotypes. We examine the simultaneous vanishing-viscosity, stiff-pressure, and continuous-phenotype limit of this system. For families of bounded weak solutions with suitable initial conditions, every sequence converges, up to a subsequence, to a continuous-phenotype incompressible Darcy system, which presents a novel biological model. This result not only addresses connections between Brinkman tissue-growth systems with discrete phenotypes and those with continuous phenotypes, but also demonstrates the robustness of such connections under both the incompressible and inviscid limits.
item.dc:creator: Chen-Chih Lai, Hongbo Lu

item.title: A decay estimate for cubic defocusing non-linear Schr\"odinger equation in three dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2512.03631v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this short note, we prove a decay estimate for non-linear solutions of the 3D cubic defocusing non-linear Schr\"odinger equation.
item.dc:creator: Yi Sun

item.title: Global controllability of the Cahn-Hilliard equation
item.description: arXiv:2512.12562v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper investigates global controllability properties of the Cahn-Hilliard equation with a standard polynomial double-well potential, posed on the $d$-dimensional flat torus $\mathbb T^d$. We first establish small-time global approximate controllability by means of controls acting on finitely many Fourier modes. The argument uses the nonlinearity constructively, through asymptotic and saturation properties, to generate new Fourier directions. We then prove null controllability of the linearized system using a spatially localized control supported on an arbitrary measurable subset of positive Lebesgue measure. The proof relies on quantitative propagation of smallness estimates and the dissipative fourth-order dynamics. For dimensions $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, we further derive local null controllability of the nonlinear equation via a fixed-point argument. Combining the global approximate and local null controllability results, we obtain global null controllability for arbitrary initial data and every $T>0$. The global control is constructed by concatenating an initial waiting stage, a finite-dimensional Fourier control, and a spatially localized control. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first results establishing small-time global approximate controllability and global null controllability for the Cahn--Hilliard equation.
item.dc:creator: V\'ictor Hern\'andez-Santamar\'ia, Subrata Majumdar, Luz de Teresa

item.title: On general Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg type inequalities involving non-doubling weights in the case of $p=1$
item.description: arXiv:2512.21492v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg type inequalities in the case of $p=1$ and generalize them adopting weight functions $w(|x|)$ on $R^n$ with $w(t)$ in ${W}(R_+)$. Here ${W}(R_+)$ is a general class of weight functions on $R_+$ including non-doubling weights like $e^{1/t}$ and $e^{-1/t}$.
item.dc:creator: Toshio Horiuchi

item.title: Global Well-Posedness of the Vacuum Free Boundary Problem for the Degenerate Compressible Navier-Stokes Equations With Large Data of Spherical Symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2601.06620v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The study of global-in-time dynamics of vacuum is crucial for understanding viscous flows. In particular, physical vacuum, which ensures a finite, nontrivial pressure-induced acceleration in the normal direction on the moving boundary, naturally arises in the motion of gaseous stars and shallow water. The corresponding large-data problems for spherically symmetric flows remain open, due to the combined difficulties of coordinate singularity at the origin and degeneracy on the moving boundary. In this paper, we analyze the free boundary problem for the barotropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations with density-dependent viscosity coefficients (as in the shallow water equations) in two and three spatial dimensions. For a general class of spherically symmetric initial densities: $\rho_0^{\beta}\in H^3$ with $\beta\in (\frac{1}{3},\gamma-1]$ ($\gamma$: adiabatic exponent), vanishing on the moving boundary in the form of a distance function, we establish the global existence of the unique classical solution with large data. Moreover, our solution is classical up to the moving boundary, and the physical vacuum is allowed for the data under consideration here when $\beta=\gamma-1$. The key ingredient of our analysis is to obtain the uniform control over the first-order spatial derivatives of the flow map $\eta(t,r)$ in spherically symmetric Lagrangian coordinates, which is achieved by some novel density-weighted estimates and flow-map-weighted estimates for the solutions.
item.dc:creator: Gui-Qiang G. Chen, Jiawen Zhang, Shengguo Zhu

item.title: On decay of solutions to the anisotropic Boussinesq equations near the hydrostatic balance in half space $\mathbb{R}_+^3$
item.description: arXiv:2601.18481v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The system of the Boussinesq equations is one of the most important models for geophysical fluids. This paper focuses on the initial-boundary problem of the 3D incompressible anisotropic Boussinesq system with horizontal dissipation. The goal here is to assess the stability property and large-time behavior of perturbations near the hydrostatic balance. By utilizing the structure of the system, the energy methods and the means of bootstrapping argument, we prove the global stability property in the Sobolev space $H^3(\mathbb{R}^3_+)$. After taking a Fourier transform in $x_h = (x_1, x_2)$ and Fourier cosine and sine transforms in $x_3$ for the system, we obtain the decay rates for the global solution itself as well as its derivatives.
item.dc:creator: Wanrong Yang, Aibin Zang

item.title: Pointwise regularity and irregularity of energy densities on $N$-dimensional Sierpinski gaskets
item.description: arXiv:2602.06642v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the pointwise regularity of energy densities associated with harmonic functions on the $N$-dimensional Sierpinski gasket $(N\ge 2)$ with respect to the Kusuoka measure. For any nonconstant harmonic function, we prove that every Borel representative of the density is discontinuous at every point of a set of full Kusuoka measure. In sharp contrast, on each one-dimensional edge of the gasket -- itself a set of zero Kusuoka measure -- the density admits a canonical pointwise version, which is $\gamma_N$-H\"older continuous on that edge with the explicit and optimal exponent $\gamma_N=\log_2 \{(\sqrt{4N+5}+1)/(\sqrt{4N+5}-1)\}$.
item.dc:creator: Masanori Hino, Kanji Inui, Kohei Nitta

item.title: Finite-energy solutions to Einstein-scalar field Lichnerowicz equations on complete Riemannian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2603.09889v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the singular elliptic problem of the form \[ -\Delta u + V(x)u = \mathcal{B}(x)|u|^{2^*-2}u + \frac{\mathcal{A}(x)}{|u|^{2^*}u}, \qquad u\in H^1(M), \] where the coefficients are allowed to have low regularity. Under natural spectral assumptions on $-\Delta+V$, geometric assumptions on the manifold $M$ ensuring the Sobolev embedding $H^1(M)\hookrightarrow L^{2^*}(M)$, and a suitable global integrability/smallness condition involving $\mathcal{A}$, $\mathcal{B}$, and a function $\psi \in H^1(M)$, we prove the existence of a nonnegative finite-energy supersolution. If, in addition, the Ricci curvature is nonnegative and $\mathcal{B}\ge 0$, we obtain a positive finite-energy solution. The proof relies on a family of $\varepsilon$-regularized problems, mountain pass arguments, and a limiting procedure in which Harnack's inequality plays a crucial role in handling the singular term on noncompact manifolds. We also prove a nonexistence result showing that the global integrability condition on $\mathcal{A}$ is, in a precise sense, necessary for the existence of nonnegative supersolutions.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: NoDEA Nonlinear Differential Equations Appl. 33 (2026), Article No. 142
item.dc:creator: Bartosz Bieganowski, Pietro d'Avenia, Jacopo Schino

item.title: Local boundedness for solutions to parabolic double phase problems
item.description: arXiv:2604.14544v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the local boundedness of weak solutions to parabolic double phase equations of type $$u_t-\mathrm{div}(|Du|^{p-2}Du+a(x,t)|Du|^{q-2}Du)=0\quad\text{in }\Omega_T:=\Omega\times(0,T),$$ where $0\leq a(\cdot)\in L^\infty(\Omega_T)$ and $\frac{2n}{n+2}<p<q<p\left(\frac{n+2}{n}\right)$, so that both the degenerate range $p\geq 2$ and the singular range $p<2$ are covered. To this end, we derive the Caccioppoli inequality and recall a parabolic embedding theorem, which are then utilized in an iteration method.
item.dc:creator: Bogi Kim, Jehan Oh

item.title: A PDE formulation of Lyapunov stability for contact-type Hamilton-Jacobi equations
item.description: arXiv:2604.24329v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Lyapunov stability of stationary viscosity solutions of contact-type Hamilton--Jacobi equations on a compact manifold. We consider Hamiltonians of the form $H(x,p,u)=G(x,p)+W(x,u)$, where $G$ is continuous, convex and coercive in $p$. We establish sufficient conditions for asymptotic stability and instability in terms of viscosity subsolutions and one-sided derivatives of a perturbed critical value. These criteria do not require the construction of a smooth contact Hamiltonian flow. Under the stability condition, solutions starting sufficiently close to a stationary solution converge to it at an exponential rate. To prove instability, we use the superposition principle for closed measures to construct calibrated curves. We also establish conditions ensuring uniqueness of stationary solutions and global asymptotic stability. Our results also cover examples with nonmonotone dependence on the unknown function, including an equation with an eikonal term $|p|$. Finally, we obtain an $O(\sqrt{\varepsilon})$ convergence rate for a class of stationary Hamilton--Jacobi equations with nonlinear dependence on the unknown function and multiscale spatial dependence.
item.dc:creator: Panrui Ni, Jun Yan

item.title: Long Time Well-posedness for the Benjamin-Ono Equation with Quasi-Periodic Initial Data
item.description: arXiv:2606.01778v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper investigates the long time well-posedness of the Benjamin-Ono (BO) equation with quasi-periodic initial data in analytic space. We demonstrate that the Lax operator of the BO equation exhibits a trivial spectrum, and elucidate the fundamental mathematical obstacles to establishing global well-posedness. Furthermore, by employing Tao's gauge transformation in conjunction with the Birkhoff Normal Form method, we extend the lifespan of the solutions to $O(\epsilon^{-3})$.
item.dc:creator: Yubo Wang

item.title: Singular stationary Navier-Stokes flows: examples and stability
item.description: arXiv:2606.22291v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Landau solutions, when oriented along the vertical axis, represent a one parameter family of exact, self-similar, axisymmetric, swirl-free solutions to the 3D stationary Navier-Stokes equations forced by an upward facing point-source of momentum at the origin. They have an isolated singularity at the origin. Other singular steady state solutions can be derived from a similar framework. Some of these variants have been proposed as models for physical scenarios. For example, a solution first found by Squire has been proposed as a model of a fluid entrained to a radially discharging surface layer of oil. Another, Serrin's swirling vortex, exhibits qualitative features shared with some tornadoes, like a two-cell structure consisting of a central downdraft and peripheral updraft as well as swirl. The first objective of this paper is to provide a detailed analysis of these and other examples, especially when boundaries are present. In this direction we find several new, physically motivated classes of solutions and identify new connections between the physics literature and the mathematics literature. Many of these examples are formulated on the half-space, but much of the mathematical literature on singular steady-state solutions is for $\mathbb{R}^3$. The second objective of this paper is to establish asymptotic stability for many of these solutions by formulating the problem in domains with boundaries. Our most general result in this direction uses a new approach to asymptotic stability that is based on eventual regularity. In a different direction, we prove that a class of singular steady-state solutions motivated by Serrin's swirling vortex are stable under certain axisymmetric perturbations. This requires a novel observation because these ``Type III'' solutions are too singular to be directly amenable to existing approaches.
item.dc:creator: Zachary Bradshaw, Dakota Palmer

item.title: Strictly stable solutions in uniformly convex planar domains may have nonconvex superlevel sets
item.description: arXiv:2607.06031v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct smooth, uniformly convex planar domains that admit minimal, strictly stable solutions of a semilinear Dirichlet problem whose superlevel sets are nonetheless nonconvex. The class of admissible nonlinearities includes, in particular, two prototypical cases: the Gelfand-type nonlinearity $e^u$ and the family of shifted power-type nonlinearities $(a+u)^p$, where $a>0$ and $p>1$. By applying the elementary scaling properties of the Dirichlet problem, we also show that the same lack of convexity of superlevel sets holds for the corresponding parameter-dependent equations. These results provide a negative answer to a question posed by Brezis, who inquired whether the stability of a solution necessarily entails quasiconcavity for these prototypical stable configurations.
item.dc:creator: Yi Ru-Ya Zhang

item.title: A note on application of mean-field limit to non-exchangeable non-conservative systems
item.description: arXiv:2607.20014v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we apply the newly developed theory of extended graphons to a certain class of non-exchangeable, non-conservative problems. We establish the mean-field limit by proving the convergence of the associated generalized weighted empirical measures.
item.dc:creator: Piotr Gwiazda, Katarzyna Ryszewska

item.title: The mean-field limit of non-exchangeable particle systems with non-conservative dynamics and adaptive weights
item.description: arXiv:2607.21110v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the paper we introduce vector-valued dynamic extended graphons in order to obtain the mean-filed limit for certain class of problems with adaptive weights. We impose fairly general assumptions on the matrix of initial connections, which allows us to cover the case of sparse graphs.
item.dc:creator: Katarzyna Ryszewska

item.title: Blow up and Concentration without Quantization: sharp Harnack type inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2607.24346v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by the Onsager statistical mechanics description of turbulent Euler flows with point singularities, we refine the blow up analysis for sequences of solutions of a class of perturbed singular Liouville equations which share the phenomenon of ``blow up and concentration without quantization". The problem is delicate because we are dealing with the exact threshold value above which one meets the well known ``concentration without quantization" phenomenon, as recently pushed forward in [C.S. Lin, G. Tarantello, {\em C. R. Math. Acad. Sci. Paris} (2016)] and in [Y. Lee, C.S. Lin, G. Tarantello, W. Yang, {\em Comm. PDE.} (2017)]. We overcome these difficulties by developing different strategies for ``fast" and ``slow" blow up, combining refined Pohozaev identities, elliptic estimates and ``Sup+CInf" inequalities in the same spirit of [C.C. Chen, C.S. Lin, {\em Comm. An. Geom.} (1998)]. In the process, we also derive a new sharp Harnack type inequality by using a moving-plane method, following the ideas in [D. Bartolucci, C.C. Chen, C.S. Lin, G. Tarantello, {\em Comm. P.D.E.} (2002)].
item.dc:creator: Daniele Bartolucci, Paolo Cosentino, Lina Wu

item.title: Gradient H\"older regularity for singular fractional $p$-Laplace equations
item.description: arXiv:2608.16243v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove interior $C^{1,\alpha}$ regularity for globally bounded weak solutions to the fractional $p$-Laplace equation $(-\Delta_p)^s u=0$ under the assumptions $n\ge2$, $1<p<2$, $0<s<1$, and $sp>p-1$, where $\alpha=\alpha(n,p,s)>0$. This resolves the open problem of gradient H\"{o}lder continuity for globally bounded solutions in the singular range $sp>p-1$. The proof is based on affine approximation and estimates independent of the normalized affine slope.
